fixes.explanation: Yes, and it's a big list. Moses says the LORD will bless “…your grain, new wine, and oil, the young of your herds and the lambs of your flocks…” and he's talking about children too. So the family, the harvest and the animals all get covered in Deuteronomy 7:13. That's a full pantry, friend.

Tents, tools and wagons never make Moses' list. He names the grain, new wine and oil, the young of the herds and the lambs of the flocks. It's all family, field and flock. I checked the list twice, and nobody gets a blessed wagon wheel.

Moses says it the other way around. He calls the seven nations “…larger and stronger than you…” (Deuteronomy 7:1). Smaller and weaker would be the nations Israel could look down on, and he never describes them that way. Somebody handed Israel the short end of the measuring stick, friend.

Even match? Oh, friend, no. Moses says these seven nations are “…larger and stronger than you…” (Deuteronomy 7:1). Nobody is walking up to a fair fight here. It's more like showing up to a bake sale and finding out the other table has a bakery truck.

That's right. Moses says, “Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.” A treaty is a deal where both sides shake hands and walk off friendly. Moses shuts that door before anybody can even knock.

That's the reason Moses gives. He says, “…they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods.” He isn't worried about the guest list. He's worried about whose voice Israel's sons would end up following. Then he says the anger of the LORD will burn against them (Deuteronomy 7:4).

Yes, loved. Moses says, “…the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers…” Israel was the fewest of all peoples, so it wasn't their numbers (Deuteronomy 7:7). I know a little about being picked when nobody was counting. A quarter, a closing bakery bin, and Mother Miller smiling at me.

Moses really does say it. He calls the LORD “…the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations…” and he says it's for those who love Him and keep His commandments. That's right there in verse 9. Nothing in it needs fixing, friend.

Moses really does say it. His words are, “And the LORD will remove from you all sickness.” That's a big promise, and he says it plainly in Deuteronomy 7:15. He even adds that Israel won't get the terrible diseases they knew in Egypt.

Moses never says shame before the nations. He says, “Do not worship their gods, for that will be a snare to you.” A snare is a trap, the kind that looks harmless right up until it snaps shut. The trap is for Israel, and that's the word he picks.

Repeat sounds close, but it isn't Moses' word. He says, “Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt…” He points to the great trials, the signs and wonders, and the mighty hand and outstretched arm (Deuteronomy 7:19). I can repeat a recipe all day and still burn the batch. Remembering is a different thing.

Moses says the opposite. He says, “The LORD your God will drive out these nations before you little by little.” He adds that Israel won't be enabled to eliminate them all at once, or the wild animals would multiply around them (Deuteronomy 7:22). So all at once isn't the plan he gives.
